Discussed integration modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC), initial success criteria, security requirements, and immediate pilot scope. SE walked through runtime config, batching and KV cache implications; customer raised questions about data residency, KMS/HSM, and latency/cost tradeoffs. Agreed on next steps: send security docs, share staging config, schedule benchmarking demo.

Pilot scope: two endpoints (customer-support summarization, fraud-rerank)
questions: Can Redwood Private be air-gapped for internal PII workflows?

How do rollbacks work if a model variant causes regression?

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-11 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Mateo (Redwood SE) -- Samantha, Derek, Priya S., Ibrahim, Maya (Newleaf)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um this is jordan from Redwood, i'll run the agenda quick, the goal is Sprint 0 kickoff, align on security, network, and scope for the pilot.
00:18 Samantha: thanks Jordan, yeah excited, we want to get the first pilot in staging within two weeks if possible.
00:25 Mateo: cool, i'll start with a quick run-through of the runtime and the typical staging config, going to call out a couple things about KV cache and batching.
00:40 Derek: quick note on our side - our infra team is on AWS in us-east-1, we have strict outbound egress policies and a corporate proxy.
00:50 Mateo: got it, we can support VPC peering or Private deployment; for hosted we do ip allowlist + managed egress options, for Redwood Dedicated you get reserved GPUs and predictable throughput.
01:05 Samantha: what's the difference, like at the level of latency and cost?
01:12 Jordan: so high level - hosted is fastest for onboarding, lower ops burden, cost per token is a little higher at low scale; Dedicated is lower unit cost at committed throughput but you have to size and commit - and Private means you manage networking and keys, most strict for compliance.
01:30 Maya: we're most worried about data residency and KMS - our security lead Priya S. is here to dig in.
01:38 Priya S.: yeah real quick, can you send SOC2 attestation and how KMS integrates? do we get HSM-level controls?
01:48 Jordan: absolutely, i'll share SOC2 and the security package after the call. for KMS, we integrate with customer KMS via the Private control plane; for hosted we use a multi-tenant KMS unless you request a dedicated key with a contract.
02:05 Samantha: the multi-tenant KMS is a no for our PII flows; we need either dedicated customer-managed keys or the Private deployment option.
02:15 Jordan: understood. we'll mark that as a must-have for the pilot.
02:25 Mateo: back to runtime - for the two pilot flows you described earlier, i recommend enabling prefix caching for the support summarization because it saves token compute on repeated system prompts. for the rerank/fraud flow, batching is key to cost reduction but we need to watch tail latency.
02:50 Derek: our SLOs: 95th pct under 300ms for the support flow; for rerank we can tolerate up to 600ms but need high throughput.
03:03 Mateo: ok that helps. prefix caching will lower p95 significantly for repeated contexts; batching will help unit cost but we may see p95 increase depending on batch window. we can tune batching windows per-route.
03:28 Samantha: is quantization an option? i know Redwood mentioned quantized model variants in the docs.
03:34 Mateo: yes - 8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants are available, but for some open models 4-bit may introduce small quality regressions; we recommend validating on your eval set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profile per workload.
03:55 Ibrahim: who on Redwood will run the initial evals with our sample prompts?
03:59 Jordan: Mateo and Priya can help; we'll need a small eval set, ideally 100-500 prompts for initial regression checks.
04:12 Priya N.: i'll coordinate collecting the eval set with Ibrahim.
04:20 Maya: network side question - what firewall ports are needed for VPC?
04:25 Mateo: typical is outbound TLS on 443 to the control plane for hosted, for Private you'll do cross-account peering and we hand you a VPC manifest; i'll drop the manifest and a short firewall checklist.
04:40 Derek: will the audit logs ship to our SIEM?
04:44 Jordan: yes, we can forward structured audit logs (S3 or syslog) and there's an option for streaming to your SIEM; we'll include details in the security package.
04:55 Samantha: timeline check - if we want staging pilot in two weeks, who's owning what?
05:01 Jordan: action: I'll send security docs and the onboarding checklist today; Mateo will share staging config and sample infra as an example; Priya (CSM) will set up access matrix and invites.
05:14 Samantha: great.
05:20 -- 05:50 (short side conversation about scheduling times; faint crosstalk)
05:50 Mateo: ok i want to briefly demo the config file - sorry it's a bit rushed - but show how you'll pin model versions, set rollout policies, and define per-route batching and cache keys.
06:08 Mateo: (screen share) so here you can see route definitions: /support-summarize and /fraud-rerank, each with a model selector, batch window ms, max batch size, and a fallback variant policy.
06:25 Derek: fallback policy - if a new variant fails qual, can it automatically revert?
06:29 Mateo: yes, we support automatic rollback if eval metrics cross thresholds or if error rate increases; you can also configure canary rollout percentages. sometimes transcript shows this as "rollout and rollback" but the automation is in the control plane.
06:48 Ibrahim: curious about cost - do you have a rough delta for hosted vs dedi at our forecasted QPS 150 req/s for rerank and 40 req/s for support?
06:58 Jordan: ballpark: hosted might be 20-40% higher unit cost initially; Dedicated becomes cheaper at steady high throughput. we'll run a quick benchmark with your sample workload to show numbers.
07:12 Samantha: ok please include cost per million tokens in the benchmark.
07:18 Jordan: will do.
07:20 Maya: ops question - will token-level breakdowns show up in console by route?
07:24 Priya N.: yes we give per-route token + latency + cost breakdowns and tracing hooks you can integrate into your tracing system.
07:36 Samantha: any blockers on compliance for private deployment?
07:40 Priya S.: we need ISO summary and evidence of key access control, and documentation about data at rest encryption.
07:48 Jordan: noted, i'll include ISO/attestation notes and the encryption architecture.
07:56 Mateo: one more thing on performance - if you go with dedicated, we often recommend a warm pool strategy. keep warm nodes to avoid cold KV cache misses on spike traffic. that reduces tail latency.
08:15 Derek: how does caching behave across replicas? is KV cache local to an instance?
08:20 Mateo: good question - KV cache is per-replica, we recommend sticky routing for flows that benefit from cache locality or use prefix caching at the edge for session-like workloads.
08:33 Samantha: do you have an example canary plan?
08:36 Jordan: yes i'll attach our canary playbook; high level: 5% traffic for 24h, monitor errors and eval metrics, then 25% for 12h, then 100% if green.
08:50 Ibrahim: what about model version pinning - can we pin model to a commit?
08:54 Mateo: yes you can pin model versions and we store immutable artifacts; you can request a rollback to a prior artifact id.
09:02 (brief pause)
09:08 Priya N.: i'll create the meeting notes and invite the infra and security folks for a deeper security session next Wednesday.
09:15 Samantha: perfect.
09:17 -- 20:00 (longer section where Mateo walked through sample metrics and a staging run; some transcription noise: "K V cash" instead of KV cache, "Redwood Dedicate" instead of Dedicated)
20:03 Derek: there's a sentence here about egress rules - we need a sample terraform template.
20:08 Mateo: i'll share a terraform snippet for the VPC peering and the security group rules.
20:18 Maya: what's the recommended instance sizing for Dedicated?
20:23 Mateo: depends on model; for MPT-like models at 8-bit, a T4 style will do for development but for production you'd want A100 or H100 equivalents - we'll propose several sizing options after we see the real throughput.
21:00 Samantha: ok if we choose Private deployment, how long does provisioning take?
21:04 Jordan: Private VPC control plane provisioning typically 5-7 business days after the contract and network handoff, on-prem can take longer - depends on your infra.
21:20 Priya S.: and audit logs retention? we require 13 months for this project.
21:25 Jordan: we support configurable retention; note longer retention is an add-on but we'll surface that in the pricing.
21:40 Ibrahim: are there any limitations on PII in training logs?
21:45 Mateo: inbound requests are not used to train Redwoods models by default; for hosted we retain minimal logs for debugging, but in Private you control retention and whether any data leaves your environment.
22:03 Samantha: good.
22:10 Derek: let's talk access - SSO integration is critical. we use Okta.
22:14 Jordan: we support SAML/Okta; Priya N will help with SSO setup steps and a runbook.
22:22 Priya N.: i'll set up an Okta app template and share.
22:30 Samantha: timeline recap?
22:34 Jordan: recap: security docs by Jordan by 9/14, staging config by Mateo by 9/16, Priya N to share invites + access matrix by 9/13, benchmark canary demo scheduled for next Friday (9/18).
22:50 Samantha: sounds good.
22:55 Ibrahim: any blockers from our legal for contract?
22:58 Jordan: legal has a standard MSA; i'll loop in our sales ops and send redline-friendly copy after the call.
23:08 (closing remarks)
23:12 Jordan: thanks everyone, Priya N will send calendar invites and notes, Mateo will upload the runbook and terraform snippet; if anything urgent ping me.
23:24 Samantha: thanks, talk soon.

End Transcript.
